contract: WHAT A 'CLAUDE IS WORKING' FRAME LOOKS LIKE, frozen here so the TypeScript scraper and the Rust
scraper fail TOGETHER rather than silently disagreeing about the same screen.
WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS (bead sparkle-s4c0xe). The two sides drifted, and the drift was invisible
for as long as nothing compared them. `statusEngine.ts` grew SPINNER_BARE_FRAME when Claude Code
2.1.237 dropped the parenthetical from its status line ('✻ Crunched for 2s'), and
`nudge_gate.rs`'s `spinner_line` never got that arm -- it still REQUIRES a parenthesised clock.
Its only other arm needs a literal '(esc to interrupt', which 2.1.237 moved into unparenthesised
chrome. So `screen_is_working` was effectively DEAD on the shipped TUI, which matters because it
is the mount-independent half: it is what can judge an agent nobody has opened.
THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENCE, which is why a shared fixture rather than two test files. A matcher
that stops matching raises no error and fails no assertion of its own -- it simply reports 'not
working' forever, and the row goes gray on a live agent. AGENTS.md records the same shape for the
Rust->TS wire payload: two halves built in parallel, both suites green, the feature never once
ran. One file, two suites, no drift.
RETUNE POINT. Claude Code rotates its glyph set and rewords its status line between releases --
2.1.218 -> 2.1.237 is this fixture's whole premise. When the wording moves, add the frame in
TODAY's shape HERE, and both languages are forced to keep up together. Do not add a frame to one
suite alone; that is the drift this file exists to make impossible.
`working` -- every one of these MUST read as 'a turn is running' on BOTH sides.
`notWorking` -- every one of these MUST NOT. These are the false-green guards: a matcher widened
until it accepts ordinary output is worse than one that is too narrow, because it paints a
finished agent green and nothing retracts it.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: 'Running 1 shell command · 1m 24s' and Claude's '◯ <kind> <label> <elapsed>'
subagent roster. Both mean the agent is busy and NEITHER scraper recognises them -- but the
roster is handled as DELEGATED WORK on its own channel (engine/backgroundTaskFooter), not as a
spinner, and listing either under `notWorking` would PIN a known gap as though it were the
intended answer. A test that pins the defect passes cleanly while the defect ships.

working.why: 2.1.237, bare, no elapsed clause at all.
2.1.237's `for <n>s` tail, which has NO parentheses — the exact shape the Rust arm missed.
The m/s arm of the same tail.
The `·` beat. Excluding it once left a whole slice of frames rejected by both arms.
2.1.218's parenthetical shape — still shipped, must not regress.
The legacy shape, carrying the interrupt hint inside the parenthetical.

notWorking.why: An ordinary finished line. The commonest false green.
A markdown bullet that happens to carry an elapsed reading. `*` is an ASCII fallback the bare arm must refuse — it is how ordinary output starts lines.
A bare glyph with no word and no clock.
